title: SearchIntent
description: Canonical fixture JSON for SearchIntent, not dataclasses.asdict() output. Python selected_providers is a tuple[str, ...]; JSON uses a string array. Python requested_geographic_scopes is tuple[tuple[str, str | None], ...]; JSON uses {provider, scope} objects. display_limit is the separate visible maximum. The acquisition-volume concepts are acquisition_budget and acquisition_requested. SearchIntent only requires a positive integer display_limit; AcquisitionBudgetPolicy is the runtime authority for supported membership (default 1 / 3 / 5 / 10, MAX_DISPLAY_LIMIT >= 10). Provider identifiers are non-blank strings; the structural PR A contract is provider-neutral and execution/policy decide support. Current BERA marketplace vocabulary is constrained on GoldenSearchCase, not here. Cross-field invariants that JSON Schema does not enforce: requested geographic scopes must belong only to selected_providers, and at most one requested geographic scope exists per provider. Those are validated by SearchIntent and by contract tests.

original_user_query.description: User query in fixture JSON. Must contain at least one non-whitespace character. The application normalizes internal whitespace, including newlines; a whitespace-only string is not a valid SearchIntent.

display_limit.description: Separate visible maximum of usable listings displayed per selected provider. Not acquisition work. Canonical fixtures use policy-supported values 1 / 3 / 5 / 10.

generation.description: Stale-response guard. A result owns the generation that produced it.

requested_geographic_scopes.description: Fixture JSON list of requested scopes. Application invariant, not encoded here: each provider must be in selected_providers, and each provider appears at most once.

scope.description: Requested geographic scope for that provider, or null when not applicable.
